transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-24
Time: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Tom Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Helix Procurement), Ethan Cole (Helix Security), Jocelyn Park (Helix Legal), Diego Morales (Helix FinOps)

Summary (auto): quick procurement check on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiers, KMS/SSO obligations, and next steps for procurement committee. Customer wants explicit egress/costing, audit-log retention, and private deployment options noted.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Tom on the technical side. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya Nair: Hey Maya, good, thanks. Busy day but we made time.
[00:11] Jocelyn Park: Hi, thanks for scheduling — we want to focus on contract tolerances rather than product demo today.
[00:16] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll keep it practical. Tom, quick intro?
[00:20] Tom Rivera: Yep hi all, Tom Rivera, SE. I'll cover technical gating items and what we can commit to from a deployment and security posture perspective.
[00:27] Ethan Cole: Great. For context, Helix is trying to decide between hosted API and a private VPC deployment. Big drivers: data residency, KMS control, and logging for auditors.
[00:37] Diego Morales: And from FinOps: predictable unit costs and explicit egress fees, we can't have surprise bills.
[00:44] Maya Chen: Understood. On the legal side, Jocelyn you sent a redline last week, correct?
[00:48] Jocelyn Park: Yes, we circled several MSA/DPA items — egress liability, data retention limits, subprocessor disclosures, and a request for an audit right. Also a clause around SLA credits and downtime definition.
[00:59] Maya Chen: Thanks. Tom, can you speak to typical SLA and what Redwood offers for dedicated vs hosted?
[01:05] Tom Rivera: Sure. Hosted API we usually publish 99.9% for inference endpoints — that's our production tier. For Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) we can negotiate a contract SLA with tighter latency percentiles and dedicated GPU pools. For Private/VPC installs, availability depends on the customer's infra; Redwood provides the control plane SLAs and support obligations but the infra-owned uptime is the customer's responsibility.
[01:28] Priya Nair: So for Private, you're saying Redwood would provide the control plane and we manage the compute in our VPC?
[01:33] Tom Rivera: We have two models: a) Private control plane with Redwood-managed images that run in your VPC, where we can offer stronger operational guarantees, or b) On-prem package where the infra is fully customer-managed — in that case our SLA is limited to the software support and security patches. The nuance is important for procurement.
[01:51] Diego Morales: For FinOps we need egress estimation up front. Does Redwood charge per-GB egress and how is that reflected on the MSA?
[01:58] Maya Chen: We'll include a clear table in the pricing addendum. Typically it's per-token for API usage + optional per-GB for raw data export/egress. For Dedicated contracts we can do committed spend with overage rates capped.
[02:10] Jocelyn Park: Legal will need the escalation path, and a maximum liability cap. Also we need to confirm whether Redwood uses subprocessors for telemetry and analytics — that is non-negotiable for us.
[02:20] Tom Rivera: We do use a small set of subprocessors for logs aggregation and monitoring; we can provide the list and offer a 30-day notice for changes. We can also support customer-managed KMS for private deployments so keys never leave your control.
[02:33] Ethan Cole: Can you confirm KMS integrations? We need AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault. Also HSM-backed keys are preferred for certain workloads.
[02:40] Tom Rivera: Yes — we support AWS KMS and have a roadmap for Azure Key Vault; HSM integration is supported on Dedicated/private when requested. We'll document the key-rotation process.
[02:51] Priya Nair: On the MSA redline, clause 6.4 about retention — we want logs retained for seven years for audit. Is that feasible?
[02:57] Maya Chen: Seven years is long; our default is one year for audit logs. For enterprise customers we can discuss extended retention as an add-on — it affects storage and cost.
[03:08] Diego Morales: Okay, if extension is possible we need a firm price delta.
[03:12] Maya Chen: We'll put a retention pricing schedule in the annex.
[03:16] Jocelyn Park: About audit rights — we prefer on-site audit or a SOC2 Type II report. Do you have attestation?
[03:23] Tom Rivera: We have SOC2 Type II reports — we'll deliver the latest attestation. For on-site audits, we typically offer a vendor audit questionnaire and a remote review; full onsite audits can be accommodated on a case-by-case basis under a higher support tier.
[03:37] Ethan Cole: Sounds reasonable. Another item: data residency — certain datasets must stay in EU-1 region. Can we pin model inference to a specific region?
[03:45] Tom Rivera: Yes, routing policies allow region pinning. For hosted customers we provision model replicas in the desired region. For Dedicated/private, you control the location. Note: not all open model variants are available in every region by default; compatibility table to follow.
[04:02] Priya Nair: Regarding pricing approval — procurement committee meets 2027-07-07. We need legal and technical clarifications beforehand.
[04:09] Maya Chen: We'll prioritize the MSA redline summary and SOC2 doc by 2027-06-26 so you have time to circulate.
[04:16] Tom Rivera: And we'll schedule a 2-hr preflight technical session the week after for Ethan and Diego to run performance runs and model validation in a sandbox.
[04:25] Jocelyn Park: On liability caps, we normally ask for a 12-month fee cap. Will Redwood accept that?
[04:30] Maya Chen: Our standard is a liability cap tied to subscription spend — often 12 months of fees for commercial customers. We can confirm exact wording once we see the final redlines.
[04:39] Diego Morales: Two concerns from FinOps: billing cadence and rate-card clarity for peak usage. We need a worked example in the pricing annex.
[04:48] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll produce a sample invoice scenario showing committed vs burst charges and egress.
[04:55] Priya Nair: Last item — can Redwood guarantee no model training on customer prompts? We need contractual language that customer data won't be used to train models.
[05:03] Tom Rivera: We already offer data non-training clauses. For hosted we'll include a DPA clause: we don't use customer content to train models unless opt-in. We'll put explicit language and telemetry options.
[05:14] Jocelyn Park: Good. That is a gating legal question for us.
[05:17] Maya Chen: Recap of next steps: Maya to send MSA redline summary + SOC2 by Saturday 6/26; Tom to schedule preflight and provide KMS/region support matrix; Priya to confirm procurement meeting date.
[05:30] Priya Nair: I'll confirm on Slack by end of day.
[05:33] Jocelyn Park: I'll aim to get top legal non-negotiables to Maya by Wednesday.
[05:37] Diego Morales: And I'll share egress numbers and current bandwidth profile.
[05:40] Maya Chen: Thank you all. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the annex documents.
[05:45] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcription has small recognition errors in product names and timestamps; several items flagged for procurement/legal follow-up.
